title: RBAC: add permissions for viewing Optimize Suggestions (Console beta)
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
## Context
Optimize Suggestions (batching/caching) is launching as a Console beta. We need a dedicated RBAC scope so orgs can limit who can view suggestions, and we must ensure strict org/project boundary enforcement (no cross-tenant leakage).

This ticket adds:
- A new permission/scope for reading suggestions
- Server-side authorization checks in the suggestions API
- Audit logging on access denials (and optionally access grants, depending on existing audit framework)
- Org/project boundary tests (unit + E2E coverage hooks)

## Proposed RBAC model
### Permission name
- `optimize:suggestions:read`

### Policy semantics
- User must have `optimize:suggestions:read` on the target project (preferred) OR the parent org with inheritance (depending on existing Redwood RBAC behavior).
- API must validate:
  1) caller identity (user/service principal)
  2) org_id + project_id scoping
  3) permission present for that scope

### API endpoints in scope
- `GET /optimize/suggestions` (list)
- `GET /optimize/suggestions/{id}` (details) if/when added; for now ensure list endpoint is fully protected.

## Acceptance criteria
1) **Denied by default**: org members without the scope receive `403` when calling suggestions API via Console.
2) **Org/project boundaries**: user cannot fetch suggestions for a project outside their org or outside their granted project scope.
3) **Audit logging**:
   - Authorization failures emit an audit event including: actor_id, org_id, project_id (if present), action, outcome=denied, reason.
   - Ensure logs do not include suggestion payload contents (avoid leaking estimated savings/risk in audit logs).
4) **Tests**:
   - Unit tests for policy evaluation & boundary checks.
   - Integration/E2E test cases for: allowed, denied, wrong-org, wrong-project.
5) **Console compatibility**:
   - Console should surface a friendly “You don’t have access” state (handled in ENG-19358), but backend must be authoritative.

## Implementation notes
- Add new RBAC constant + documentation in the authz registry.
- Update suggestions service handler to call `requirePermission(optimize:suggestions:read, org_id, project_id)`.
- Confirm whether Console uses project-scoped token vs org-scoped; implement accordingly.
- For multi-project orgs, confirm if suggestions are computed per project+route. Enforce the same scope as the underlying telemetry/cost views.

## Security considerations
- Treat suggestions as potentially sensitive (reveals usage patterns / internal routing names / cost signals).
- Avoid side-channel leakage:
  - `404` vs `403`: prefer consistent behavior per Redwood conventions. (We currently return `403` for known resources; confirm with Marcus.)
  - Do not include org/project existence hints in error messages.
- Ensure stable IDs cannot be enumerated across tenants; ID lookup must always check org/project scope.

## Rollout
- Ship behind the Suggestions beta feature flag.
- Coordinate with support on access requests and expected error states.

## Links
- ADR (API contract + stable IDs): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-suggestions-api-contract-and-stable-ids.json
- Runbook (API latency/error triage): sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-suggestions-api-latency-and-error-triage.json
- E2E test plan: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/suggestions-view-e2e-test-cases.json

## Notes / open questions
- Should we include an additional scope for “apply” actions later? (Out of scope for beta; view-only scope now.)
- Should read access be bundled with existing Optimize view scopes? Current guidance: keep Suggestions explicit to reduce accidental exposure.

2026-01-24 (Marcus Lin): Prefer `403` when the caller is authenticated but lacks permission; ensure message is generic. For non-existent IDs, `404` is fine, but do not leak cross-tenant existence. Gate lookups by org/project before checking existence.

2026-01-28 (Felix Schneider): Suggestions API currently only lists by org_id+project_id; please ensure both are required inputs server-side (don’t allow org-only list unless explicitly requested). UI always calls with project context.
2026-02-03 (Chloe Martin): Make sure audit event does NOT log the request query filters if they include route/model names. Those can be business sensitive.
2026-02-08 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implemented permission checks and added audit log on denied. Added unit tests for org/project boundary and role inheritance behavior. Sending for review.

2026-02-12 (Dylan Brooks): Please align denial audit event naming with the console-cost endpoints (same schema). Also confirm that service principals (CI tokens) are either blocked or explicitly supported.

2026-02-14 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Updated audit event naming to `authz.access_denied` and added `resource=optimize_suggestions`. Service principals: allowed if granted permission in RBAC (matches other Console read endpoints).
2026-02-21 (Chloe Martin): Verified in staging with two test orgs. Cross-org enumeration attempt returns 403 with generic message; no payload leakage. Good to close once E2E tests land in ENG-19501.
